title: Bughouse at Vineyard Theatre #bughouse #henrydarger #vineyardtheatre ...
transcript: How could such an interesting figure give way to such an uninteresting play? Unfortunately, this question continually swirled around in my head during this new show at Vineyard. In it, we see the peculiar and enigmatic Henry Darger, a man whose traumatic life filled him with big ideas and led him to become a prolific artist and writer. This piece is primarily a rehash of the ideas and core memories that plagued him and ultimately manifested themselves in his art. John Kelly's portrayal of Henry Darger is fine but lacks nuance, as there's practically no room to characterize him within the confines of this piece. It's a lot of tedious narration, coming in at about 60 minutes but feeling longer. Despite all of the cool lighting effects and projections, they don't necessarily augment the storytelling — they feel more like a pacifier to compensate for the otherwise dry production. My biggest gripe though is that this play doesn't reveal anything about Henry Darger that you can't get from reading a biography, or for that matter, the program note. I wonder how this would’ve been had it examined his art as a way to interpret his life, rather than the other way around. With that, another program for my collection.
